title: Observer
objective: Let one object announce a change to many listeners without knowing who they are.

sources.title: Gamma, Helm, Johnson and Vlissides, Design Patterns (Addison-Wesley, 1994): the Observer pattern

simplifies: Listeners here run one after another in the same process. Real systems often put events on a queue (see Message queues), so a slow or failing listener can't hold up the order or the other listeners.

steps.caption: When an order ships, Order itself calls email, SMS and analytics, one by one.
Order now depends on every class that cares about shipping.

predict.prompt: Marketing wants a WhatsApp message when an order ships. Which class changes?

options.text: Order, which has nothing to do with WhatsApp
options.explanation: Right. Order names every listener, so every new listener edits it.
Order still has to call it.
Analytics only tracks; it doesn't send messages.

steps.caption: Observer: Order keeps a list of listeners. Anything with notify() can subscribe; Order calls them all when something happens.
Order ships and tells the first listener…

predict.prompt: Who decided which listeners Order tells?

options.text: Whoever subscribed them, usually at start-up
options.explanation: Right. Order just loops over its list; it never names a listener's class.

options.text: Order, by checking each listener's class
options.explanation: Order only knows that each one has notify().

options.text: The listeners poll Order every second
options.explanation: They don't poll; Order calls them when it changes.

steps.caption: …and the last. Adding WhatsApp is a new listener that subscribes itself; Order doesn't change.

exercise.change: Also add loyalty points when an order ships.
exercise.hint: Which class calls every interested party by name?

options.text: Have Order keep a list of listeners and notify them all; Loyalty subscribes itself
options.explanation: Right. Order announces; whoever cares listens.
Loyalty isn't a kind of order, and it still wouldn't hear about shipping.

options.text: Have Loyalty check the order's state every few seconds
options.explanation: Polling wastes work and can miss quick changes: the problem Observer solves.

exercise.explain: Order only knows the Listener interface. Loyalty implements notify() and subscribes, so the change is a new class and nothing that exists has to change.

quiz.prompt: In Observer, what does the subject (Order) know about its listeners?

options.text: Only that each one has notify()
options.explanation: Right. That's what keeps it decoupled.

options.text: Each listener's class and what it does
options.explanation: Then every new listener would mean editing Order.
It keeps a list of them and calls notify() on each.

quiz.prompt: In a simple loop, one listener throws an error inside notify(). What can happen?

options.text: The listeners after it never hear about the event
options.explanation: Right. That's why real systems catch errors per listener, or use a queue.
An uncaught error stops the loop.
Nothing undoes the shipping; the other listeners just miss the news.
